shared_elements: grid of rectangular glyph blocks in rows and columns
rounded-cornered cartouche signs with internal faces/eyes
frontal human/deity face with elaborate headdress (B; face-like signs in A)
framing border band around carved panel
justification: Both surfaces carry the same distinctive convention of square-cornered cartouche signs packed into ordered rows and columns, each filled with rounded, face-like or dotted internal motifs, and both frame the carved field with a border band; B additionally combines this glyph grid with a frontal figure in an elaborate headdress set in a niche above the text, whereas A shows only the glyph grid with no figural scene visible.  The shared sign-block grammar and rendering conventions are specific enough to suggest a common tradition, but the presence versus absence of a large central figure is the main difference in depicted content.
